summary: 赵高弑二世后立，在位四十六日，诛高降汉，旋为项羽所杀；未称帝号，图鉴作准帝。
summary_en: Installed by Zhao Gao after the murder of the Second Emperor, he reigned forty-six days, slew Gao, surrendered to Han, and was put to death by Xiang Yu; never bearing the imperial title, the gazetteer lists him as quasi-emperor.

portrait.appearance_basis: 史载无形貌描写。画像宜表现亡国之际仓皇受玺的宗室之态，衣冠从秦制。属艺术想象。

timeline.title: 赵高立子婴
timeline.summary: 赵高弑二世，立子婴，去帝号称王，秦政尽在赵高。
timeline.summary_en: Zhao Gao murdered the Second Emperor, set up Ziying, and dropped the imperial title for that of king; all Qin governance lay in Zhao Gao's hands.

timeline.title: 诛杀赵高
timeline.summary: 子婴与其二子及宦者韩谈谋，刺杀赵高于斋宫，夷三族。
timeline.summary_en: Ziying conspired with his two sons and the eunuch Han Tan, struck down Zhao Gao in the fasting palace, and exterminated his kin.

timeline.title: 降刘邦
timeline.summary: 刘邦入武关至霸上，子婴系颈以组、奉玺降于轵道旁，秦亡。
timeline.summary_en: Liu Bang entered by the Wu Pass and came to Bashang; Ziying, a silk cord about his neck, surrendered with the seals beside the Zhidao road, and Qin was no more.

timeline.title: 秦王非帝
timeline.summary: 子婴去帝号称秦王，不系帝统，图鉴以名分不成立而作准帝。
timeline.summary_en: Ziying bore the title of king, not emperor, and so stands outside the imperial line; the gazetteer treats him as quasi on grounds of title.

timeline.title: 项羽杀子婴
timeline.title_en: Xiang Yu Puts Ziying to Death
timeline.summary: 项羽入关屠咸阳，杀子婴，烧秦宫室，秦社稷绝。
timeline.summary_en: Xiang Yu entered the pass, sacked Xianyang, killed Ziying, and burned the Qin palaces; the Qin altars were cut off forever.

timeline.title: 子婴总评
timeline.summary: 国祚短促而能诛高，然承积弊、无兵可恃，终不免于亡。
timeline.summary_en: His reign was brief yet able to slay Zhao Gao; but he inherited a broken state without troops to lean on, and ruin was not to be escaped.

relations.note: 二世被弑后，赵高立子婴
relations.note_en: After the Second Emperor is assassinated, Zhao Gao enthrones Ziying

relations.note_en: A Qin imperial clansman; the records differ on his origins (son of the Second Emperor's elder brother / younger brother of the First Emperor)

bio_md:
# 秦王子婴 · 主要事迹

子婴身世史有异说——或云二世兄子，或云始皇弟，或云扶苏之子；《史记·秦始皇本纪》称其「仁俭，百姓皆载其言」。二世三年，赵高弑二世于望夷宫，欲自为帝而群臣不从，遂立子婴，去帝号称秦王。赵高挟子婴与之约：「且称王，以顺民心。」然子婴知其奸：即位五日，即与其二子及宦者韩谈设谋，于斋宫刺赵高，夷其族，尽诛于咸阳。

诛高之后，秦已无可挽之局。刘邦破武关、下蓝田，兵至霸上；子婴系颈以组，白马素车，奉天子玺符，降于轵道旁。秦之社稷，历二世而亡，子婴在位仅四十六日。其后项羽入关，屠咸阳、烧宫室，杀子婴，秦之宗庙遂绝。

子婴以末代秦王入史，未称帝号，名分不系帝统，图鉴以准帝收录。其诛赵高之决，足称危局之能，然承焚书坑儒之弊、当六国并起之势，纵有贤主亦难挽回，史家多寄惋惜之意。秦之亡与其人无关，亡在始皇二世之暴政，此可为子婴平反者。

> 参考：点校本《史记》卷006《秦始皇本纪》、卷008《高祖本纪》、卷007《项羽本纪》。

bio_parts_en.value:
Ziying's parentage is disputed in the histories — some call him the Second Emperor's nephew, some the First Emperor's younger brother, some Fu Su's son; the *Shiji*'s "Basic Annals of Qin" records that he was "benevolent and frugal, and the people all praised his words." In the third year of the Second Emperor, Zhao Gao slew the Second Emperor at Wangyi Palace and, failing to take the throne himself against the ministers' will, set up Ziying, dropping the imperial title for that of king. Ziying knew his malice: on the fifth day of his reign, plotting with his two sons and the eunuch Han Tan, he stabbed Zhao Gao down in the fasting palace and exterminated his kin in Xianyang.

With Gao gone, Qin was past saving. Liu Bang broke the Wu Pass, took Lantian, and came to Bashang; Ziying, a silken cord about his neck, riding in a white-draped cart and bearing the imperial seal, surrendered beside the Zhidao road. The Qin altars, after two emperors, were no more — Ziying had reigned forty-six days. Xiang Yu then entered the pass, sacked Xianyang, burned the palaces, and put Ziying to death, cutting off Qin's ancestral sacrifices forever.

Ziying enters the histories as the last king of Qin. He never bore the imperial title and stands outside the imperial line, so the gazetteer lists him as quasi-emperor. His resolution in slaying Zhao Gao shows a ruler equal to a desperate hour; but inheriting the ruin of the book-burning and scholar-burying age, against the converging six states, even a worthy sovereign could not have turned the tide. The historians' regret is a vindication: Qin fell not by his hand but by the tyranny of the First and Second Emperors.

> References: the punctuated critical edition of the *Shiji*, ch. 6 ("Basic Annals of Qin"), ch. 8 ("Basic Annals of Gaozu"), ch. 7 ("Basic Annals of Xiang Yu").
